card.name: Words after 'lowest' before dose terms
card.fires_on: Mostly the word right after 'lowest' or 'commercially' (such as available or recommended) in dosing and drug-description text. It also fires weakly on scattered linking words in science prose.

modes.label: Lowest available/recommended dose
modes.description: The adjective after 'lowest' that comes just before the word dose.
modes.example: start with the lowest<< recommended>> dose and titrate while monitoring for safety

modes.label: Drug availability or origin
modes.description: A modifier after an adverb in describing a drug, such as available or originally.
modes.example: lapatinib, a commercially<< available>> inhibitor of ErbB2 and EG

modes.label: Scattered linking words
modes.description: Short function words in general science text, such as 's, that or a.
modes.example: transform the genes<< that>> synthesize cinnamon oil into E. coli

card.plain: It marks the word that finishes a phrase like 'lowest recommended' or 'commercially available' just before a drug or dose noun.
